caption:
Google announced the Fitbit Edge, a $179.99 fitness tracker with a bigger AMOLED screen, built-in GPS and up to a week of battery life.

Pre-orders are open now, and it reaches shelves October 27. Buyers get three months of Google Health Premium, which includes Google's AI health coach.

Would you trade a smartwatch for a tracker like this?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Google, 9to5Google · Photos: Google

slides.headline: Google launches the *$179.99 Fitbit Edge* with a week of battery life

slides.heading: A *bigger screen* on a slim tracker
paras: The Edge has a wide AMOLED display with 46% more screen than the Charge 6. The aluminum body is 11.5 millimeters thick.
It comes in four finishes, with swappable bands from $39.99. A Stephen Curry edition costs $219.99.

slides.heading: Battery you can *replace*
paras: Google rates the battery at up to seven days. Five minutes on the magnetic charger adds about a day of use.
Google calls it the first repairable Fitbit tracker, with a battery owners can replace.

slides.heading: GPS, ECG and an *AI coach*
paras: Built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than on the Charge 6, and the tracker supports more than 50 exercise modes plus an ECG app.
AI-powered activity detection recognizes over 100 workouts. Google's AI health coach requires a paid Google Health Premium plan.

paras.t: Buyers get three months of Premium free.

slides.hook: AI is moving onto your wrist. Follow for every wearable launch that matters.
